observations.surface: Package manifest Elysia declaration and install
observations.atomic_claim: Input: parsed target package.json. Expected: both peerDependencies.elysia and devDependencies.elysia use a semver range satisfied by 1.3.0 (for example ^1.3.0); a fresh install with elysia@1.3.0 resolves one copy and new Elysia().use(partyserverMiddleware()).handle(GET /health) returns the downstream 200 response.

Input: parsed target package.json. Expected: peerDependencies.partyserver equals the baseline range '>=0.2.0 <1.0.0'; installing partyserver@0.5.10 with elysia@1.3.0 resolves the package and routePartykitRequest remains importable and callable at runtime.

Execute this concrete behavior and verify the handling path uses the required target technology. Scope: packages/hono-party/src/index.ts; surface: Error propagation without ctx.onError. Behavior: If processing throws Error('boom') and ctx.onError is absent, app.handle resolves to Elysia's 500 error response for that thrown error and the downstream route is not called.. Required postcondition: Given a fresh Elysia app with partyserverMiddleware({ options: { onBeforeConnect: () => new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 }) } }) registered before any route, app.handle(new Request('http://localhost/parties/chat/room', { headers: { Upgrade: 'websocket' } })) resolves to a 401 Response with body 'Unauthorized' and no downstream route runs; the Hono source instead returns null from handleWebSocketUpgrade and falls through because the Response has no webSocket handle.. Use the same semantic predicate in both environments; source must fail the target condition, target must satisfy it. A missing target capability is a semantic failure; an unrelated setup or execution error is not.

Execute this concrete behavior and verify the handling path uses the required target technology. Scope: packages/hono-party/src/index.ts; surface: Non-upgrade response passthrough. Behavior: When routePartykitRequest returns new Response('hello', { status: 201, headers: { 'x-custom': 'v' } }) for a non-upgrade GET, app.handle returns status 201, header x-custom value v, and body 'hello' unchanged.. Required postcondition: With E = { Bindings: { JWT_SECRET: string } }, onBeforeRequest(req, lobby, c) observes c.env.JWT_SECRET === 's3cr3t' from the current Cloudflare environment and c.request.url === 'http://localhost/parties/chat/room' from the current Elysia PreContext; the Hono source exposed hono Context.c.env instead.. Use the same semantic predicate in both environments; source must fail the target condition, target must satisfy it. A missing target capability is a semantic failure; an unrelated setup or execution error is not.

Execute this concrete behavior and verify the handling path uses the required target technology. Scope: packages/hono-party/src/index.ts; surface: GET /parties/chat/room. Behavior: A GET /parties/chat/room carrying Upgrade: websocket with both hooks configured invokes onBeforeConnect exactly once and onBeforeRequest zero times.. Required postcondition: Given app.use(partyserverMiddleware({ options: { onBeforeRequest: () => { hits.push('hook'); } } })).get('/parties/chat/room', () => { hits.push('route'); return 'routed'; }) with routePartykitRequest returning null, app.handle(GET /parties/chat/room) produces hits ['hook','route'] and body 'routed'; a plugin registered after the route would produce ['route'] only.. Use the same semantic predicate in both environments; source must fail the target condition, target must satisfy it. A missing target capability is a semantic failure; an unrelated setup or execution error is not.

A missing target capability is a semantic failure; an unrelated setup or execution error is not.
